subject: genetics
question: **Type:** application A single eukaryotic gene produces three different mRNAs in three different tissues, and each mRNA is translated into a different protein. What mechanism accounts for this?

options.text: The gene is transcribed in different directions in different tissues.
RNA polymerase reads a different template strand in each tissue.
Each mRNA is produced from a different allele of the gene.
Alternative splicing joins different combinations of exons from the same pre-mRNA.

explanation: Alternative splicing allows the same pre-mRNA to be spliced into different exon combinations, so one gene can encode multiple proteins in different cell types. A is wrong because a gene is always transcribed in one direction from the same promoter. B is wrong because the same template strand is read in every tissue. C is wrong because one gene, not several alleles, is the source of all three mRNAs.
